memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Jethro was delighted to hear about all the good things the LORD had done for
Israel in rescuing them from the hand of the Egyptians." - Ex 18:9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Jethro was delighted. Not envious, not indifferent, not competitive. Delighted.

This is a small verse with a large heart in it. Jethro was a Midianite priest.
The blessing being described was not his people's blessing. Israel's rescue did
nothing for Midian's standing in the world.

And he was glad anyway.

That is harder than it sounds. Hearing about someone else's blessing, especially
when your own situation has not changed, tests something in us. Paul's
instruction to "rejoice with those who rejoice" (Rom 12:15) is often more
difficult than mourning with those who mourn. Grief invites sympathy naturally.
Someone else's good news can quietly expose our own discontent.

Notice what Jethro was delighted about specifically: "all the good things the
LORD had done." His joy was fixed on God's goodness, not on comparing outcomes.
That is probably the secret of it. When we are genuinely glad that God is good,
we can be glad He has been good to someone else.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Whose good news is hard for you to celebrate honestly?
2. Can you be glad about God's goodness even when your own situation is
   unchanged?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, free me from comparing. Give me genuine delight when I hear of Your
goodness to others. Amen.
